text: Databases store and organise information so that applications can find and use it quickly. There are two main types: SQL and NoSQL. SQL databases keep data in tables with rows and columns, which makes the structure clear and easy to understand. To get information, you write queries, which are simple instructions that ask the database questions. Good data modeling is important because it decides how the tables connect to each other. Indexes also help a lot: they work like a book's contents page, so the database can find data faster without searching every row. Choosing between SQL and NoSQL depends on your needs.
